summary: Successive observations of two luminous phenomena in the sky with sudden disappearance: probable observations of reflections on aircraft.
description: A driver and passenger on the A6 motorway were surprised to twice observe a stationary luminous phenomenon in the sky, approximately 30 degrees above the horizon. The phenomenon disappeared suddenly without a trace. While of low oddity, this relatively precise observation is classified as a probable observation of sunlight reflecting off high-altitude aircraft. This case is classified as Class B.

summary: Multiple observations of the rapid passage of a luminous phenomenon across the night sky: probable observations of atmospheric reentry.
description: On December 23, 2008, several witnesses in different French departments observed a brief passage of a luminous phenomenon in the night sky. Four reports were collected. All four reports from that day (Labarthe-Inard (31), Aureil (87), Roquelaure (32), and Le Vigean (86)) support the observation of a fireball (visual appearance, brief duration of one to a few seconds). The available azimuth and elevation information (of varying accuracy depending on the report) allows us to define an area of overlap located, a priori, in northern Spain (see the PowerPoint presentation of the four reports and the fireball summary document). The only inconsistency concerns the heading (i.e., the direction of movement). The witness in Le Vigean indicated North-South, while the other three indicated East-West. However, it is quite common in confirmed fireball sightings to have discrepancies in heading due to the brevity of the observation (still compatible with a good position reading in the sky, but less so with its heading). It can also be noted that three observers place the sighting close to 10 PM, while one of them (Aureil (87)) mentions 9 PM. Seven years later, it is difficult to resolve this discrepancy through a new appeal for witnesses. GEIPAN classifies this case as B: probable fireball sighting.

summary: Observations of the silent movement of three luminous yellow-orange spheres. Probable Thai lanterns.
description: On December 21, 2008, at 7:46 PM, a driver and his passenger noticed an intriguing phenomenon in the sky. After parking the car, the witnesses observed three circles of yellow-orange light moving silently for several minutes. The description of the phenomenon—three orange orbs moving for a few minutes in the direction of the wind (a light westerly wind that evening, see weather report)—perfectly matches the characteristics of Thai lanterns. The witnesses' account provides details that reinforce this hypothesis: "equipped with a ring," "yellow-orange in color, like a lighter flame." The time (7:46 PM) and day (Sunday) are unusual, but it could have been a test run for a larger display planned for the end-of-year holidays. Although the witness does not approve of this hypothesis, this case is class "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Photograph of the zigzag movement of a luminous object.
description: On December 19, 2008, GEIPAN received an email concerning an attached photograph: a week before Christmas, a witness observed and photographed the rapid, zigzag movement of a luminous phenomenon. The date of the photograph, extracted from the photo's EXIF data, indicates that it was taken on December 19, 2008, at 9:24 PM. Cases of Thai lanterns moving in Réunion were reported to GEIPAN on December 14 and 16, 2008. No further details were provided by the witness. No other reports of this phenomenon were received that evening.

summary: Observation of bluish lights.
description: On December 18, 2008, between 5:58 and 6:05 AM, a witness was intrigued by a noise and bluish lights in the sky and over their garden. The observation lasted one minute. The witness thought something was slowly flying over their house. Frightened, this person alerted their husband, who was downstairs, but the lights had disappeared in the meantime. No other reports of this phenomenon were collected in the area, and the witness provided too few details to support any hypothesis. This case is classified as C due to lack of information.

summary: Observation of the movement of a luminous phenomenon.
description: On the evening of December 16, 2008, between 8:45 and 9:00 PM, two witnesses observed the rapid movement of a luminous phenomenon. A very bright red glow moved silently and along a random trajectory above the city of Saint-Pierre. The object was sometimes obscured by clouds. No other reports of this phenomenon were recorded that evening. However, during the same period, the movement of Thai lanterns was observed by numerous witnesses in different locations on the island. The witnesses likely observed a Thai lantern, also known in Réunion as a "wish lantern" or "Chinese hot air balloon."

summary: Observation of a Thai lantern passing by.
description: On December 14, 2008, at approximately 9:00 PM, several witnesses observed the silent passage of an orange spherical object for 20 seconds. It moved from east to northwest in a straight line without leaving any trail. The object disappeared after a flicker of brightness. One of the witnesses stated that similar orbs had been seen the previous week. The Makes Observatory, contacted about this, referred to them as "Christmas lanterns" of the same type as Thai lanterns. This hypothesis was confirmed by the main witness, who observed them again on Christmas Eve.

summary: Observation of the slow movement of three luminous points. Triangular formation: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On Saturday, December 6th, at 10:18 PM, a witness observed three bright, orange-red lights moving silently and in unison across the sky, following a northwest to southeast trajectory. The witness had just enough time to take three photos before the phenomenon was obscured by the building's roof. A fourth object with the same characteristics was then observed, moving along the same trajectory. The entire observation lasted approximately fifteen minutes. The observed characteristics (orange-red color, slow and straight movement consistent with the wind direction, within a few degrees) strongly suggest a misidentification as a flight of festive lanterns (known as Thai or Chinese lanterns). The time and date (Saturday after 10 PM, Saint Nicholas Day, a holiday widely celebrated in Alsace) are perfectly consistent with this hypothesis. This type of observation is a classic example of a misidentification of festive lanterns. This case is class B as a very probable sighting of festive lanterns.

summary: motorist briefly observed a green light with a crescent-shaped trail passing over a downhill curve: probable atmospheric reentry.
description: On November 12, 2008, at approximately 10:40 PM, a motorist observed a green light passing on a downhill curve, followed by a crescent-shaped trail. The sighting lasted only a few seconds. The witness's account is consistent, and the phenomenon is corroborated by two other independent witnesses (found on a forum) who were located far away, and even by a radio recording (see the investigation report). This sighting corresponds, as the witness suspected after some research, to the atmospheric reentry of a meteor. In reality, it originated from the Northern Taurid meteor shower, which produces impressive, relatively slow-moving fireballs. The daytime also coincides with the peak activity of this shower, which, as observed elsewhere, was active at that time. Two eyewitness accounts from the Bordeaux region, consistent in time, description, and trajectory, confirm, given the distance between Bordeaux and Carspach, that the UFO was necessarily at high altitude. This further strengthens the hypothesis. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: meteoroid reentry.

summary: Observation by a witness of two fixed bright points in the sky before their simultaneous extinction: probable observation of weather balloons.
description: On Friday, November 7, 2008, at 6:25 p.m., a witness was waiting for his partner to go to a show. He went outside to observe the sky and noticed two unusual, fixed points of light in the east. As his partner arrived, the points slowly went out. The observation lasted a few minutes. Two high-altitude weather balloons could very well have produced this appearance: the observation took place about an hour after sunset; at altitude, the balloons were still in the sun; their simultaneous extinction, with their entry into shadow, is perfectly logical. This entirely plausible hypothesis, however, could not be confirmed by GEIPAN (the French National Astronomical Investigation Group), as it was too long after the event. This case is classified as Class B: probable observation of two weather balloons.

summary: Observation of the slow movement of a black triangle with white lights on the vertices for 5 to 10 seconds: lack of information.
description: On November 4, 2008, at 7:52 PM, a motorist observed a black triangular object with two white lights at two of its vertices moving slowly for 5 to 10 seconds. This observation suggests a low-flying aircraft, but this seems highly unlikely in that location. This case of observation is of low strangeness (slow-moving white lights) and low consistency (inconsistent weather conditions and a very short observation period for a witness in motion in their vehicle). This case is classified as Class C due to a lack of information.

summary: Presence of an unknown object in an amateur video.
description: After acquiring a new camcorder, an individual tested it by filming a helicopter. Upon reviewing the footage, he noticed a gray sphere throughout the recording. Unfortunately, the witness did not wish for his film to be released, even though it is an excellent example of this type of phenomenon. This video shows, with near certainty, a very small object passing very close to the lens, without necessarily being noticed by the operator, most likely an insect or a bird. This type of document (photo or video) is quite common since the advent of digital cameras, particularly compact cameras, whose very short focal length means that such small objects are not completely blurred and therefore "diluted" into the background, as they would be in film photography or traditional video.

summary: Observation of a luminous phenomenon followed by a black triangle passing slowly over the rooftops.
description: Testimonies collected in November 2009 regarding an earlier observation made in October 2008 (the witness no longer remembers the exact date but indicates the end of October). Around 6:00 AM, two witnesses got into their utility vehicle and began their rounds. They first noticed a very bright phenomenon, like a star, and then, above the houses of the village they were driving through, they saw a huge black triangle with a red light in the middle. This observation includes two phenomena that are not necessarily related: - The white point of light, seemingly too bright to be considered Saturn, which is nevertheless in a nearby direction. - The black triangle with a red light: one might think of an airplane, but the witness reportedly observed one of the navigation lights and, more importantly, the flashing of the anti-collision lights. It is noted that the movement of this object would be consistent with that of a conventional aircraft: it is its shape and lighting that make it unusual. The late date of the report prevented verification with aviation authorities. This sighting is of medium to high strangeness, and the investigation conducted has considerably strengthened its credibility. None of the usual hypotheses adequately explain the observation of the triangular object described by the witnesses. This case is classified as "D1" as unexplained.

summary: Observation of two bright red spots.
description: Recent report (April 19, 2010) of an old observation. On September 28, 2008, a witness observed two bright red points in the sky for approximately 15 minutes. One of the points moved slowly, then accelerated before disappearing. The stationary light described could correspond to the planet Venus, visible to the naked eye in the west at sunset (orange-red light) with a magnitude of -4.2. The "red planet," Mars, was not visible to the naked eye (apparent magnitude of +1.5, too low on the horizon). The second moving red light could be an aircraft. However, as this is an old observation reported several months later, any verification or investigation is impossible. The case is classified as Class C due to lack of information.

summary: Multiple observations in France of the passage of a luminous phenomenon in the night sky: observation of the atmospheric reentry of a 3rd stage of a PROTON launcher.
description: On September 25, 2008, around 11:00 PM, numerous witnesses in southern Brittany and southern France saw a spectacular luminous phenomenon cross the sky from the northeast to the southwest. Many reported their sightings to the press and to GEIPAN (the French National Center for Information on Astronomical Phenomena) by telephone (5), email (5), or questionnaire (3); some filed a report with the gendarmerie, which then forwarded three testimonies to GEIPAN. The numerous witnesses described a very powerful luminous phenomenon that crossed the sky in 1 to 4 minutes (for most), heading south or southwest (see the investigation report). We have compiled the essential elements of these observations in a single table (attached). We can observe a great deal of variability in these elements, both in the color of the phenomenon (white, yellow, orange, red) and in its shape (sphere, point, rocket-like plane, and even rectangle), the estimated distance (300m to 8 km), the direction of movement (mostly from North to South, or Northwest to Southeast, West to East), and the duration of observation (mostly less than 1 minute, with a few cases exceeding 2 minutes). Nevertheless, the simultaneity of the phenomenon, and some common characteristics such as fragmentation into more than 10 elements, leave little doubt as to the single origin of the phenomenon (except perhaps in the case of Pontoise). Experience shows that such variability is frequent for all mass observations; It is also important to consider that all the witnesses, being geographically dispersed, did not see the phenomenon from the same angle or for the same duration: this leads to a perfectly explainable variability in the witnesses' accounts. In this type of case, it is the number of witnesses at the same time and their significant geographical distance that proves that the phenomenon was very powerful and at high altitude: the atmospheric reentry hypothesis becomes certain. The nature of the reentering object is more difficult to prove: in this case, due to the phenomenon's southeastward orientation and its duration of less than a minute, the hypothesis of a satellite debris re-entry is much more likely than that of a natural meteor re-entry. Information from American space surveillance has confirmed this hypothesis. This case is therefore classified as A: atmospheric reentry of a 3rd stage of a PROTON launcher.

summary: Observation of the silent passage OE of a luminous point at constant speed in the sky: observation of the international space station (ISS).
description: This observation, on September 25, 2008, at 9:00 PM, of a large bright point crossing the sky from west to east in a few minutes at the beginning of the night suggests the observation of a large satellite passing overhead. A check on the Calsky website indicates the International Space Station (ISS) passed overhead a few minutes before the time indicated by the witness (see report). The witness specifies that he had already seen the same phenomenon several times in previous years and months; this statement is consistent with this hypothesis. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of the International Space Station (ISS). Note: the same evening at 11:00 PM, a much more spectacular phenomenon was visible in the same region: the re-entry into the atmosphere of a third stage of a Russian PROTON launcher.

summary: Probable successive observations of the ISS
description: witness reported successive observations on September 21, 2008, and July 10, 2009, of luminous spheres moving silently. A set of photographs taken by the witness is attached to their description. This case concerns observations made by the same witness on several dates without any official police report. These observations are described as single or faint points of light and paired structures in the questionnaire returned by the witness to GEIPAN (the French National Group for the Study of Astronomical Phenomena). Given the number of observations, GEIPAN commissioned an IPN (National Paranormal Investigation) specialist who focused on the first observation of September 21, 2008. The reported elements suggest a probable observation of the International Space Station (ISS). The description of "spheres" and a "central core" is due to the use of optical instruments (binoculars). This case is classified as Class B.

summary: Observations of the movement of about ten luminous orange balls in the sky: observation of Thai lanterns.
description: From September 20th to 21st, 2008, a witness observed about ten orange orbs in the night sky moving between the towns of Gouvieux and Precy-sur-Oise. These luminous orbs, "lit from within as well as on all sides," disappeared near Precy-sur-Oise. The objects moved silently in a line at low altitude. Only one witness statement was collected by GEIPAN (the French National Gendarmerie's Office for the Study of Unidentified Aerial Phenomena). The gendarmerie received two other calls that night regarding the presence of lights in the sky. The witness's observation is characteristic of a Thai lantern release, in terms of colors, shapes, and trajectory. The fact that it occurred on a weekend night, a time conducive to festive events, reinforces this hypothesis. The general east-west direction of the movement is consistent with the measured wind direction. Furthermore, the local gendarmerie report mentions sightings at the same time that are also characteristic of Thai lanterns. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as category B – observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the movement of about thirty luminous objects in the sky.
description: On September 7, 2008, at 12:20 a.m., a witness photographed luminous objects in the sky from their garden. The witness has since consulted recent photos of confirmed cases of Thai lanterns and recognizes the similarity of the observation. This case is classified as Class A: high probability of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observations of different luminous phenomena appearing successively. Lack of information.
description: On September 5th or 6th, 2008, between 10:30 PM and 11:00 PM, several people observed luminous phenomena moving across the sky in the direction of the Col de Braus. One witness (the exact date is unclear) reported the successive appearances of colored luminous orbs, some of which seemed to rotate. Two other orbs were moving parallel to each other at high speed. No unusual noises were heard during the observation. This observation was a succession of three phenomena that we consider independent: a bright orange point of light on the western horizon, slowly disappearing after 30 minutes: this could be the star Arcturus at sunset (see astronomical charts at 10:30 PM and 11:00 PM), very bright, close to the direction indicated by the observer. Bright white balls moving erratically against the cloudy background: this description perfectly matches the appearance of a disco laser, although the observer doesn't see the upward beam (this is always the case, except in very humid atmospheres). Finally, the very rapid, straight passage of two bright points: this phenomenon clearly suggests the atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid (fragmented meteorite) or space debris. Given the uncertainty surrounding the date and the lack of evidence for these hypotheses, GEIPAN currently classifies this rather unusual case as "C" due to a lack of information. The strangeness of the case stems primarily from the succession of these three phenomena.

summary: Observing the flight of a kite.
description: On August 30, 2008, at approximately 7:50 PM, a witness observed a flying object he could not identify. He took a series of photographs and filmed the object's movement. (The film was never sent to GEIPAN). Following a neighborhood inquiry, the police investigation concluded it was a kite. Indeed, kite enthusiasts regularly fly at the stadium in the town of Ablis. This was confirmed by several witnesses that day, one of whom reported seeing a kite particularly high in the sky.

summary: Observation of the evolution in the night sky of a yellow colored ball: probable observation of a Thai lantern.
description: On Saturday, August 30, 2008, at 11:45 PM, a witness was stargazing when his attention was quickly drawn to a yellow sphere, slightly to the left of his eye, surrounded by multicolored glitter. He observed it through binoculars and confirmed that it was a yellow sphere with multicolored lights inside. Initially, the sphere was stationary for two to three seconds. It then slowly began to move, gaining speed. It first traveled horizontally, then started to descend diagonally until he lost sight of it, as the Montcy-Notre-Dame forest is located opposite his home. He left for ten seconds to go to the bathroom. His friend, who was present, called him to inform him that the ball had returned to its original starting point at the time of its first appearance. It retraced its exact same path and then disappeared behind the forest. The witness's observation (yellow ball), the movement consistent with the light prevailing wind (westerly) noted that day on Météociel, the time and day of the week (Saturday evening), and the presence of a nearby festival (Le Cabaret Vert) are consistent with the observation of several Thai lanterns. Indeed, the observed colors and glitter can be explained by the observation of the lantern's flame (flickering) and envelope, which are different colors. The impression that the lantern returned to the same spot after the observation was interrupted is probably due to the presence of a second lantern following the same air current. Furthermore, at that time lanterns were less widespread; the year 2008 marks the beginning of observations (see case LANTERNS 03.05.2008 on the GEIPAN website). In conclusion, this is likely an observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Brief observation in the night sky of the movement of a white light: lack of information.
description: On August 29, 2008, at 10:45 PM, a witness looked out of a closed window and was intrigued by the presence of a white light resembling a star, but much brighter, in the Northwest. The observation lasted approximately 6 seconds, during which the witness saw the UFO move, stop, and then disappear. No other eyewitness accounts have been collected. This testimony is not particularly unusual. The various descriptions also refer to a star. The lack of unusualness might stem from this description ("stationary, then slightly accelerated, then stationary again"), which is inconsistent with another ("The phenomenon moved slowly northward, then stopped and disappeared"). Furthermore, the duration of the observation was short (6 seconds). It is also worth noting that this testimony was given nearly 18 months after the sighting. Overall, GEIPAN considers that it does not have enough reliable information to draw a definitive conclusion. Nothing excludes a star (the proximity of a moving cloud can give the impression of movement before the gradual fading, interpreted as rapid movement over distance) or a Thai lantern. GEIPAN classifies this case as C: lack of information.

summary: Observation of an object in the sky and photographs of the UFO: probable observation of a balloon.
description: A witness contacted GEIPAN by email regarding an observation of an object in the sky over Fechain on Friday, August 15, 2008, around 6:30 PM. He attached three photographs but provided no other documentation to clarify his observation. No other reports were collected about this phenomenon. This observation is entirely consistent with the sighting of a balloon. GEIPAN therefore classifies it as a B case, indicating a probable balloon sighting, and not as an A case, due to the inability to definitively prove its origin.

summary: Observations of a fixed black spot on the sun.
description: In a phone call, GEIPAN was informed that numerous people had been observing a stationary black spot on the sun since late August, particularly in the late afternoon. No further reports or information were received to supplement the phone call. Due to a lack of additional information to date, this phenomenon is classified as Class C.

summary: Astronomical observation.
description: On August 10, 2008, GEIPAN (the French National Center for Experimental and Astronomical Research) was contacted by telephone by a witness who reported an observation made in the presence of other people, including police officers. Between 11:00 PM and 2:17 AM on the night of August 10-11, 2008, two bright points, resembling stars, were observed first with the naked eye and then with binoculars. The phenomenon was stationary at first and then moved slowly. A similar observation in the same direction, but slightly lower on the horizon, occurred on August 22 at 10:35 PM. The investigation revealed that the witnesses had made an astronomical observation of Arcturus and Capella, which are particularly visible at this time of year.

summary: Observation of 9 bright spots outlining triangular formations: lack of information.
description: witness reported a five-second observation made on July 31, 2008, at 11:15 PM in a private garden. The witness observed nine non-flashing points of light moving silently from east to west across the starry sky. These points, grouped into three triangles, formed a triangular shape that suddenly began to rise before disappearing. No other reports of this phenomenon were collected. The witness, who clearly saw a strange phenomenon, was very impressed by their observation. The movement of the lights was not consistent with the wind direction, which rules out the possibility of Thai lanterns. This case was submitted to the experts at GEIPAN. The report contains few concrete details, and there is only one witness, making it a case of weak consistency. Therefore, this case is classified as "C": observation not actionable due to lack of information.

summary: Observation of a dark, lenticular-shaped mass moving across the sky: probable sighting of a balloon.
description: On July 30, 2008, at approximately 10:05 PM, two people from their 6th-floor apartment observed an unusual object to the left of the Eiffel Tower: a dark, lenticular-shaped mass, initially stationary, then moving towards Charles de Gaulle Airport, merging into the horizon before disappearing in a flash of light. The witness filmed the observation, first at 10:05 PM and then again at 10:08 PM. Of low to moderate strangeness, and with good video quality, this observation strongly suggests a small balloon accidentally licked in the Parisian sky, especially given its movement, which is entirely consistent with an object carried by the wind. Although the witness testimony does not entirely support this hypothesis (the flash), this case is classified as Class B: probable balloon sighting.

summary: Observation of a luminous phenomenon and circular shapes present in photographs but without visual evidence.
description: On April 23, 2009, the mayor of a small town submitted a CD and a letter addressed to the town hall to the gendarmerie. The CD contained two photographs taken on July 27, 2008, by a vacationer passing through the area. A black object is visible in the landscape in one of the photos. No one in the town reported any unusual sightings that day. The photographer went to the gendarmerie on August 11, 2009, to report an observation made during his vacation on July 27, 2008, at 10:45 a.m., and the discovery of a sphere and a disc in photographs taken that day. The witness stated that he noticed nothing unusual while taking the photos. Without direct visual evidence of the phenomenon at the time of taking the photos and without any other eyewitness accounts or information, any investigation into this phenomenon is difficult, if not impossible.

summary: Observation of the slow and silent movement of an object: observation of an airplane.
description: On Sunday, July 20, 2008, at 10:12 PM, a driver and his passenger observed a mysterious shape moving for about a minute. An elongated, light gray, matte object with two large tail fins made a loop and disappeared to the west. Two photographs were taken with the witness's cell phone. No other witness statements were collected, and no unusual aerial phenomena were reported in the area. The conclusion of the police investigation is plausible: a passenger plane making a sharp turn to align itself with the runways of Roissy-Charles de Gaulle International Airport.

summary: Brief observation of a large, elongated, dark triangular shape delimited by non-flashing yellow-orange lights: observation of Thai lanterns.
description: witness reported an observation made during the night of Sunday, July 14, 2008 (between midnight and 12:05 AM) in a clear, cloudless sky. He observed above his home the silent passage of a large, dark, triangular shape moving southwest to northeast, bordered at each end by large, round, non-flashing, yellow-orange lights. The witness went outside, but the UFO had disappeared. Only one witness account was collected. Considering the following objective factors: clear weather, good visibility, dark night; light winds; trajectory of the UFO(s) consistent with the local wind direction; short duration of the observation; several large lights seen by the witness, but perceived as a single object; dark orange color; relatively moderate brightness of the UFO; observation made during a three-day weekend coinciding with a national holiday. It is reasonable to conclude that the witness most likely observed several Thai lanterns (or festive illuminated balloons) carried together by the wind, giving the impression of a single object. These lanterns were launched either from Saint-Malo itself, or from Dinard or one of its beaches, on a Sunday evening in summer, the eve of a national holiday. GEIPAN classifies the case as A: observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Teche in a photograph.
description: A witness sent us a photograph showing a teche. This photograph is unusable, and we lack information regarding the sighting itself.

summary: Observation of a bright point seen with the finder scope of an astronomical telescope.
description: On July 8, 2008, at 9:25 PM, from the summit of Bergies Mountain, witnesses were intrigued by a bright point of light that appeared and disappeared several times in the sky. The witnesses located it using the finder scope of a telescope. Taking turns, they looked through the finder scope and described an ovoid object, steel gray in color, moving slowly (with a pendulum-like motion for one of the witnesses). The object moved southward before disappearing. This case is highly unusual due to the shape of the object observed through the 9x50 finder scope of the telescope. It is also quite plausible, as the witnesses are experienced and skilled in intensive observation, both day and night. The investigator dispatched to the site by GEIPAN found nothing abnormal and confirmed the testimony and good faith of Mr. A (Mr. B was not present during his visit a month after the sighting). This case is classified as D1, unexplained sighting, moderately strange, of good consistency.

summary: Multiple observations of the movement of luminous phenomena in formation: flight of the Patrouille de France.
description: On July 2nd and 4th, 2008, between 10:15 PM and 10:45 PM, several witnesses in the Apt area of the Vaucluse region observed unusual movements of luminous phenomena. Lights appeared and disappeared in formation over a period of 20 minutes. No noise was heard during the observations. One witness filmed the phenomenon on July 4th, and another took photographs. The investigation established that these individuals had witnessed a night flight by the Patrouille de France (French Air Force aerobatic demonstration team) during a training exercise over Apt on the evenings of July 2nd and 4th, between Saint-Saturnin-lès-Avignon and Fontaine-de-Vaucluse. The timing of the witness statements is consistent with the flight times (July 2nd was for a rehearsal for a ceremony that took place on July 4th). The Patrouille de France aircraft are Alpha Jets equipped with a landing light in the nose, which is illuminated during flight displays to ensure visibility. On these evenings, the Patrouille de France conducted holding patterns in the area, flying in formations of eight aircraft before the display and then four aircraft before beginning their approach procedure at Salon-de-Provence Airport, thus confirming the reported observations. This case is the subject of a separate news item on the website.

summary: Element in photograph without direct visual: probable passage of insect.
description: A witness sent us one of their photographs, surprised to find an element they hadn't seen when the picture was taken. This photo, taken without direct observation, shows a gray trail following a point of light and is likely the result of an object passing very quickly close to the lens. Indeed, the object is very blurry. It is probably an insect briefly illuminated by the camera's flash (the EXIF data indicates that the flash was triggered). This case is classified as "B": probable photograph of an insect, with flash.

summary: Observation and photographs of a luminous phenomenon moving across the sky: lack of information.
description: Following a press article, GEIPAN decided to investigate an observation made on June 23, 2008, at 4:52 a.m. by a witness who took photographs of a luminous phenomenon in the sky. According to the investigation report, there are numerous inconsistencies in the testimony (photography conditions, other witnesses untraceable), and a strong correlation between the diameter of the photographed object and the Moon (however, GEIPAN was unable to reproduce this nebulous appearance and its colors). The evidence is far too weak and questionable for this case to be considered substantial. It is classified as C due to a lack of reliable information.

summary: Sky lantern observation.
description: On June 22, 2008, at approximately 1:30 a.m., two witnesses observed about ten orange lights moving across the sky. The witnesses heard no noise and filmed the phenomenon. Thanks to the clear video footage and following a police investigation, the person responsible and the location of the sky lantern release were identified.

summary: Observation in the countryside of a strong yellow glow moving silently and appearing to follow the witness's vehicle: lack of information.
description: On June 19, 2008, at approximately 10:30 PM, two people on a country road observed a powerful, round, yellow light directed towards the ground, slowly moving in clockwise circles. No unusual noises were heard; the phenomenon disappeared as they entered the village. This sighting is of medium to high strangeness, but its lack of consistency, due to the insufficient detail in the simplified questionnaire provided online by a UFO association, as well as the absence of other eyewitness accounts, makes it impossible to classify it as a D1 case. Pending further potential eyewitness accounts or an on-site investigation, this case is classified as C due to the lack of corroboration with other independent reports.

summary: Probable sighting of Thai lanterns.
description: On June 13, 2008, at 11:30 PM, witnesses observed luminous phenomena moving from their homes. A video showed bright lights moving from northeast to northwest. Other people in the street also saw the lights, and numerous internet users reported seeing them on various websites. The large number of luminous objects moving along the same trajectory and with low luminosity was likely due to the release of Thai lanterns during a festive event. Those responsible for and the launch sites of these lanterns are very difficult to find, and we encourage anyone involved in this type of activity to contact GEIPAN.

summary: Old observation of the passage of three ovoid objects in the cloudy sky: lack of information.
description: On August 3, 2009, a witness contacted GEIPAN regarding an earlier observation made on June 3, 2008, at 9:00 PM. From a third-floor balcony, the witness observed the successive appearance of three objects, roughly the shape of a rugby ball and brown and pale yellow in color. The objects moved along a straight trajectory, two of them in the same direction. No noise was heard during the observation, which lasted about ten seconds: the phenomenon disappeared from view through clouds. Ultimately, this observation of ovoid objects appears to be of low to moderate strangeness, with a fairly probable hypothesis of the observation of aircraft perceived with a particular shape and brightness due to the time being close to sunset (14 minutes later). The investigation, which was too late, did not allow for confirmation of this hypothesis; therefore, this case is classified as C due to a lack of information on aircraft flights at that time.

summary: Successive observations of a luminous phenomenon.
description: Successive observations of a light that moved and changed intensity. Despite several prompts, the witness did not provide any further details, including the date (the day is not specified in the correspondence and is given here arbitrarily). Any investigation is impossible.

summary: Successive observations of the movement of luminous phenomena: probable observations of aircraft landing lights seen from the front.
description: In 2009, a person reported successive observations from their home. They testified to the presence and movement of balls of light seen near Charles de Gaulle Airport. The witness filmed their observations between 11 p.m. and midnight during the first days of summer, at the end of June 2008 (the date of June 21st is given arbitrarily). The videos show yellow-orange lights slowly descending towards the ground. As the witness claims to be observing in the direction of the airspace surrounding Charles de Gaulle Airport, these lights are probably the landing lights of aircraft approaching the airport. These lights are visible to the aircraft up to approximately 30 km away: therefore, their color can vary from white to yellow-orange depending on the distance and atmospheric turbulence, and several aircraft can be observed simultaneously, the distance of which, even relative, cannot be estimated. Due to perspective, these points may appear to move closer together at the point of contact or further apart. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable observation of aircraft approaching head-on, close to landing. Since the witness did not provide precise dates or directions of observation, GEIPAN was unable to refine the investigation.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of a large white light followed by a smaller red light: lack of information.
description: Following a televised report about lights in the sky, a witness claims to have seen, on May 31, 2008, between 10:30 and 11:00 PM, along with other people, a large white light followed by a smaller red light, moving silently one behind the other before disappearing. This testimony is quite unusual, and the description too brief for a serious study. The witness did not respond to our request for a questionnaire or to file a statement with the police. It could simply be satellite passes and/or sky lanterns, but the lack of detail in the testimony prevents us from verifying either of these hypotheses. Due to insufficient information, GEIPAN classifies this case as "C".

summary: Probable atmospheric reentry of a meteorite.
description: On May 30, 2008, at 2:00 a.m., a witness observed a green light in the sky for a few seconds. A ball of light appeared to fall from the sky and then disappeared abruptly. No further information was gathered. This person likely witnessed the atmospheric reentry of a meteorite.

summary: Successive observations of luminous phenomena in the sky: astronomical observations followed by observation of the passage of the international space station.
description: witness reported successive observations of luminous phenomena in the sky, notably on May 29, 2008, the silent movement of a luminous yellow-white sphere. The witness described two easily identifiable phenomena. The stars that changed color were simply twinkling due to high-altitude winds; this effect depends on the day's weather conditions and can be more or less pronounced. The UFO, visible as a bright, luminous sphere, was very likely the ISS (International Space Station), which passed over the Breton sky at the time indicated by the witness (see the document "ISS Calsky Passage"). The report was sent on May 30, and the witness stated "last night," therefore it was indeed the night of May 29-30, 2008. Given the lack of precision in the report, this hypothesis, although very probable, cannot be definitively confirmed. This case is class "B": probable observation of the International Space Station ISS.

summary: Probable passage of the International Station.
description: On May 28, 2008, at approximately 12:04 AM, a witness observed a bright object rapidly passing across the sky. Its straight trajectory was northwest. This witness likely observed a pass of the ISS (see the direction and times of ISS passes over France on that date. The time given is GMT + 2 hours (French summer time).

summary: Successive observations of blue shapes in the cloudy sky: probable observation of nighttime lighting on clouds.
description: witness briefly reported by email repeated sightings of more or less round blue lights in the cloudy skies of the Paris region. The witness sent photographs. No other reports were collected regarding this phenomenon. The photograph strongly suggests the reflection of ground-based lighting on the clouds, which is hardly surprising: although the witness's precise location and the direction of observation are unknown, the Paris region is full of lights from monuments, town halls, and, of course, nighttime establishments whose powerful spotlights are lost against the cloud cover. This is a likely case of mistaken identity involving reflections of lights on the clouds. The very low oddity of this case does not warrant further investigation. This case is classified as Class B, probable observation of nighttime lighting on clouds.

summary: Passage of the ISS (International Space Station).
description: On May 12, 2008, between 10:40 PM and 10:45 PM, a witness observed a luminous object crossing the sky from south to northeast. This white, very bright object moved rapidly, following a curve in its trajectory. No sound was heard. After investigation and confirmation by the French Meteor Observation Network (REFORME), this phenomenon turned out to be a pass of the ISS (International Space Station), visible in Aubagne between 10:42 PM and 10:47 PM on that date, and which can now be particularly bright since the installation of the four pairs of solar panels (its magnitude can be significantly negative, down to approximately -4).

summary: Successive observations in the sky of bright points varying in size and intensity: probable observation of military aircraft on exercise.
description: On May 21, 2008, between 11:30 p.m. and 12:20 a.m., a witness observed a luminous phenomenon moving across the sky. Intrigued, he observed the phenomenon through binoculars and then filmed his observation. Because the video leaves little doubt as to the object observed—an approaching aircraft, seen head-on, with all lights on—and because this area is likely a training zone for tactical transport aircraft, GEIPAN classifies this case as B, indicating a probable observation of military aircraft during training exercises. It should be noted, however, that the 50-minute duration of the observation is inconsistent with the sequence described by the witness: either the witness saw more than two aircraft passes, which remains consistent with the hypothesis, or he misjudged the total observation time.

summary: Observation of the passage of a luminous phenomenon: lack of information.
description: witness briefly reported their observation on May 21, 2008, around 11:00 PM. From their garden, they observed a small sun moving linearly from southwest to northeast, approximately 30 arcseconds above the horizon. Its speed was constant. The phenomenon then moved eastward before quickly disappearing. This somewhat unusual account suggests a Thae lantern (a flying lantern carried by the wind), but it is too brief to allow for a precise analysis against which to compare the usual hypotheses of misinterpretation. Weather stations surrounding the observation site reported contrary winds, which can be explained by the passage of a front visible in satellite images. In any case, the precise weather conditions at the location are unknown (nearest station: Caen, 50 km to the northeast). This case is classified as Class C due to a lack of information.

summary: Red stains on the photograph.
description: witness sent us a photograph showing red spots. After analyzing the photograph, it turned out that the red spots were reflections of streetlights inside the camera lens. If each streetlight is connected to a red spot, the three lines intersect at a point that is the "mirror" point of the phenomenon. This mirror point is located exactly in the center of the photo, which therefore corresponds to the focal point of the lens. Each red spot has an intensity related to the distance of the streetlights in the photo, and thus their brightness varies. This phenomenon is quite common, but this photo is truly a textbook case, probably because the three streetlights are grouped around the optical center of the lens.

summary: Observation of the ballet of luminous orbs in the cloudy sky: probable projections of lights (sky rose type)
description: On May 17, 2008, between 10:35 PM and 11:15 PM, two people observed, at low altitude in the cloudy sky, the spectacle of three luminous orbs merging and multiplying. This observation is very likely a case of mistaken identity with the light projected onto the clouds by a "Sky Rose" type lighting system, similar to the observation made in the same direction on the D101 road from Servon-sur-Vilaine towards Châteaugiron the previous night (see Châteaugiron (35) case, May 17, 2008). This case is classified as Class B, probable observation of light projections (commercial promotion).

summary: Observations of the movement of two opaque white masses in the sky: probable observations of light animations with a Sky Rose type projector.
description: On May 17, 2008, at approximately 1:45 a.m., several people in a vehicle observed a mysterious luminous phenomenon in the sky: two opaque white masses of light moving across the sky. They changed shape, appearing and disappearing for a few seconds. Curiosity, sparked by a recent local newspaper article, excellent visibility, and the increasing sophistication of light show projectors surprised the witnesses to the point that they reported what was almost certainly a case of mistaken identity involving a Sky Rose projector. Another witness very likely saw the same thing the following night (Cesson-Sévigné (35) case, May 17, 2008). GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Sky Rose-type light shows.

summary: Observation of the movement of a luminous ball behind clouds: lack of information.
description: On May 16, 2008, around 11:00 PM, a witness observed a luminous sphere moving from left to right behind the clouds. This testimony is not very unusual, and the description is too brief for a serious study. The witness did not respond to our request for a questionnaire and to file a statement with the police. The limited information provided leaves open the possibility of numerous well-known phenomena. Due to a lack of precise data, GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" for insufficient information.

summary: Observation of the slow and silent movement of three luminous yellow-orange balls in the night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On May 14, 2008, between 9:30 p.m. and 10:30 p.m., during a birthday party, three people observed three luminous yellow-orange orbs slowly moving along an east-west axis. No sound was heard. The observation lasted less than a minute. Only one witness statement was recorded. The witness's observation is characteristic of a Thai lantern release, in terms of colors, shapes, and trajectory. The general east-west direction of the movement is consistent with the wind direction measured in Avignon at 10:00 p.m. (east wind). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Spot on photo without observation at the time of shooting.
description: On May 12, 2008, around 6:00 PM, someone took two photographs of Fort La Latte. Upon later reviewing these photographs, a black teche appeared in one of the two photos, even though no observation had been made during the taking of the pictures. Numerous hypotheses could explain a teche in a photograph without direct observation, and are therefore unverifiable.

summary: Observations of the rapid passage of a dark, triangular mass at low altitude. Probable observation of an aircraft.
description: On May 11, 2008, at approximately 10:50 PM, two witnesses observed a dark, triangular mass with steady and flashing white, green, and red lights moving at high speed across the sky. During the observation, which lasted several tens of seconds, a faint, low-pitched noise was heard. This earlier sighting, in addition to the primary witness, led to several other reports following press coverage. Ultimately submitted to the panel of experts working with GEIPAN (the French National Gendarmerie Intervention Group), this case, with a low level of strangeness, was classified as Class B, indicating the probable sighting of an aircraft, a hypothesis suggested by one of the spontaneous witnesses. This case is a typical example of misidentification/confusion when describing aircraft lights (a misunderstanding between flashing and steady white, green, and red lights).

summary: Observation of particular shapes in a photograph after the fact: probable passage of insects.
description: A witness reported their astonishment after discovering unusual shapes in photographs. This case, without direct observation during the photography, presents all the characteristics of a post-hoc misidentification: a pair of insects passes very quickly and very close to the camera lens, resulting in a blurring effect while the rest of the image is sharp. This case is class B.

summary: Observation of the movement of a red object in the sky.
description: On May 10th, around 11 PM, a witness observed a red object in a clear, starry sky from their garden. The object moved rapidly from south to west. The witness went home to get their camera. In the meantime, the object disappeared, but the witness still managed to take a photograph, which the next day showed a white object near a star. The information provided by this single witness appeared contradictory and lacked precision (no statement was given to the police and no observation questionnaire was completed), making the investigation difficult and impossible to draw any conclusions.

summary: Observation of the passage of 2 orange balls in the night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: A brief email reports an observation made on May 10, 2008, around 11:30 PM in Avignon. A witness saw a bright flash in the clear, storm-free sky. Ten seconds later, the witness observed a round, orange object moving from the north, followed by another similar object. Both objects moved southeast before disappearing. Only one witness account was recorded. This case is very poorly documented: just three lines in the witness's email. The witness's observation is characteristic of a Thai lantern release, in terms of color, shape, and trajectory. The direction of movement perceived by the witness, from north to southeast, is consistent with the wind measured in Avignon that day (originating at 40° East), given that the UFO appeared to pass east of the witness without passing directly overhead (the witness was looking out the window). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as category B: Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the passage of a luminous phenomenon. Passage of the ISS.
description: On May 8, 2008, at 4:30 AM, two people observed a very bright, white, oval-shaped object moving from west to east across the sky. That day, the International Space Station (ISS) was visible, rising at 4:27 AM (SW) at 225° N and setting at 4:37 AM (East) at 70° N (source: Winstars). The observation of a bright point of light moving from west to east for approximately two minutes at 4:30 AM corresponds to the ISS passing at its brightest point, particularly since the addition of extra solar panels (magnitude -4).

summary: Observation of the EO passage of a luminous phenomenon: probable atmospheric reentry.
description: On May 7, 2008, at 1:30 a.m., two witnesses observed a round, white object at an altitude and distance they could not determine. The object moved rapidly from east to west on a slightly downward trajectory. No sound was heard. Only one of the witnesses reported the sighting. These individuals likely observed an atmospheric reentry of a meteorite.

summary: Observations of the silent movements of two luminous balls in the sky: lack of information.
description: On May 7, 2008, at 10:55 PM, a group of six high school students observed two luminous orbs in the sky. The orbs moved silently, appeared stationary, and then quickly resumed their upward trajectory. The map of the scene and the weather report (light easterly wind in Nantes) suggested the possibility of Thai lanterns, which could have been released from one of the houses on the edge of the forest to the east. However, the witness account did not entirely support this hypothesis: white and blue orbs, a luminous thread, and a movement that was not perfectly linear. Given the relative incongruity of the case and its age, GEIPAN (the French National Group for the Study of Unidentified Aerial Phenomena) did not reopen the investigation. GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of information, although the Thai lantern hypothesis remains quite plausible.

summary: Observation of the movement of an orange ball in the sky.
description: On the night of May 6, 2008, at 11:58 PM, two people observed a very bright orange ball moving north from their home. The ball then disappeared, hidden by the landscape. Whether or not there was any sound accompanying the ball has not been confirmed. No other accounts have been gathered regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observation of the ES displacement of a luminous ball: probable mistaking for Jupiter.
description: On May 8, 2009, GEIPAN received a brief email regarding an observation that occurred during the night of Monday, May 5 to Tuesday, May 6, 2008, between 3 and 4 a.m. No further details were provided. The direct testimony contained too few details for a proper analysis. Jupiter was present in the Southeast (azimuth 128° and 3°48' elevation) and could be a source of confusion, especially since the witness did not mention it. The perceived movement could be due to autokinetic illusion: see the link: The perception of the movement of a point of light in the sky. This case is class B: probable misidentification with Jupiter.

summary: Observation of the passage of a luminous sphere.
description: On May 5, 2008, between 7:00 and 7:05 AM, a motorist and his daughter observed a luminous sphere passing at high altitude for a few seconds. The phenomenon quickly disappeared behind the clouds. No other accounts were collected regarding this phenomenon, for which we lack information.

summary: Probable sighting of Thai lanterns
description: On Sunday, May 4, 2008, between 10:45 and 10:50 PM, two people observed three yellow-orange light sources moving from their terrace for fifteen seconds. No sound was heard. These lights moved slowly from west to north before suddenly disappearing. This observation followed many others during the same period in western France. Many of these observations have been explained by the release of Thai lanterns. The description given by the witnesses, the behavior of the lights, their yellow-orange color, and the day of the observation (a Sunday evening) suggest that we were also witnessing a flight of three Thai lanterns, probably released during a family celebration.

summary: Observation of the rapid movement of two bright points above the horizon.
description: On May 4, 2008, at approximately 4:30 a.m., a witness observed two bright points of light moving very rapidly above the horizon for about 10 seconds. A few seconds later, these points separated and moved in opposite directions. No sound was heard. No further details were gathered about this phenomenon, for which we lack information.

summary: Possible sighting of flying lanterns.
description: On May 4, 2008, at approximately 10:45 PM, a motorist observed about ten luminous orange orbs motionless in the sky for five minutes. No unusual noise was heard. Despite the limited information provided by the witness regarding this phenomenon, it is likely that this person observed sky lanterns. Indeed, numerous such sightings were reported between May and July 2008 in eastern France.

summary: Observation of Thai lanterns passing by
description: On the night of May 3, 2008, starting at 10:00 PM, numerous witnesses along the Atlantic coast and on the Île d'Yeu observed several luminous orbs moving in the sky. No unusual noises were heard during these observations. These sightings were reported by the local and national press. One person contacted the local gendarmerie on the Île d'Yeu to claim responsibility for these luminous phenomena. That evening, at a private party, around 10:00 PM, they had launched Thai sky lanterns, a type of hot air balloon that drifts with the wind and currents before extinguishing, from Pointe du Cantin in the northwest of the Île d'Yeu. These sightings were the subject of a specific news item on the GEIPAN website.

summary: Successive observations of silent movements of luminous shapes in the sky: probable observations of a Sky Rose type laser beam animation.
description: On Friday, May 2, 2008, at approximately 11:15 PM, a driver and his passengers observed a rapidly moving white light phenomenon in the sky. An oval shape was seen with several bright points of light rotating inside. Another observation occurred later that same night around 2:00 AM. No noise was heard during either observation. The family observed the phenomenon again on Saturday, May 10, 2008, at 2:30 AM. This observation is not unusual: the hypothesis of a nightclub spotlight is entirely consistent with the observation. The indicated direction of observation (Northeast on page 2, then North on page 3) does not allow us to determine the origin of the probable light that was observed. This case is therefore classified as Class B: probable observation of commercial projections, such as those used by nightclubs.

summary: Observation of a pyramidal object five meters above the ground. High-pitched voices and incomprehensible words heard; violent headaches: lack of information and cross-checking.
description: On May 1, 2008, at 10:15 PM, a young teenager outside his home heard high-pitched voices and unfamiliar words before seeing an unidentified object suspended in the air, about five meters above the ground. The witness described the dark-colored object as pyramidal in shape, large in size, and topped with a bright beam of light. Different colors were also visible. The object remained stationary. The witness believes he stared at this sight for perhaps 15 or 20 minutes. He was then blinded by a bright flash, and when he opened his eyes again, the object had disappeared. The witness then experienced severe headaches, which subsided upon the arrival of his brother. Another witness reported to the police that on the same evening, in the same area, between 9 and 10 p.m., his dog had barked abnormally, whereas it usually only barks in the presence of visitors. This observation is highly unusual, as it involves a close observation of a completely unknown phenomenon, coupled with the hearing of entirely unfamiliar sounds. The witness and his family filed a report with the police. The police conducted a thorough investigation and found no traces on the ground, nor any confirmation of aircraft flights in the area at that time. GEIPAN contacted the witness by telephone in 2011 to inquire whether he had received any updates on his experience, or if it had recurred; but there was no new information on these matters. This observation report has none of the characteristics of a hoax. GEIPAN searched the local press to see if there had been any other similar accounts in the region at that time. GEIPAN consulted a doctor who stated that, "in ophthalmic migraines, visual phenomena (scintillating spots, geometric shapes) precede severe headaches, which seems to be the case for this young man. The attack occurs abruptly, without any initiating factors. It can be frightening and very anxiety-provoking. The age and sex are consistent with this diagnosis." This hypothesis cannot be confirmed, but must be considered. As in all cases of very strange observations by a single witness, it is very difficult to confirm the reality of the observed phenomenon, even if the witness is considered sincere. Because the account contains certain elements characteristic of a transient hallucination, GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of concrete evidence and corroborating reports.

summary: Observation of a luminous ball in the sky.
description: On May 20, 2008, a witness reported via email having seen a luminous sphere a few days earlier (he no longer remembered the exact date), initially stationary and then moving silently northward. The testimony was too brief (the precise date was unknown) to allow for any investigation, but the observation was similar to those of Thai lanterns seen in the region around the same time.

summary: Probable sighting of a Thai lantern.
description: After reading an article from May 8, 2008, about luminous orbs, someone reported observing a sort of luminous 3D diamond in the sky around 11 p.m. on the night of May 1-2, 2008. Moving north without any sound, it disappeared over the horizon. This person likely witnessed the passage of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of the movement of a bright white point in the sky: probably a Thai lantern.
description: On May 1, 2008, between 11 PM and 1 AM, a fisherman on a beach observed the slow movement of a white light in the sky, which appeared to originate from the Île d'Yeu and move eastward. The witness lost sight of the light as it drifted into the clouds. This observation has the characteristics of a Thai lantern: a luminous sphere moving with the (east) wind. The date and time are consistent with this hypothesis: it could have been a lecher launched from a boat at sea. The observed northward deviation is probably an effect of the cete wind, which alters the wind flow at low altitude. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a Thai lantern.

summary: Separate observations of two low-altitude luminous phenomena, no noise: lack of information.
description: On May 8, 2008, GEIPAN received by email a brief description of two sightings that had taken place on the evening of Tuesday, April 29, by a driver (T1) and his passenger (T2). At the entrance to the hamlet of La Chalousière in the commune of Vallet (44), they observed a luminous phenomenon at low altitude, consisting of two lights. Just after dropping his colleague off at her home, T1 quickly made a second observation of a slowly moving, very low-altitude object illuminated by colored lights. No unusual noises were heard during either sighting. T1 reported his two sightings in a questionnaire on January 8, 2009. No other reports were collected. Given the objective elements analyzed, namely: - An apparently stationary object, similar to an aircraft approaching the witnesses on an axis close to or identical to their axis of movement, - The presence of two or three powerful lights, similar to aircraft landing lights, - A dark night with cloud cover layered on two levels, making it difficult to clearly distinguish the aircraft's outline on the one hand and obscuring it at times on the other (according to the Nantes METAR bulletin SCT012 and BKN055, there were scattered clouds (3/8 to 4/8) at the ceiling located at 1200 feet (350m) and very cloudy skies (5/8 to 7/8) at 5500 feet (1700m), we can conclude that this observation probably concerns only one or two aircraft on approach to Nantes-Atlantique Airport with their landing lights on. This case is to be classified as a case of... lack of precise information on the exact time (around 9pm or 10pm), the precise locations of observation (especially for the second observation) and the directions of observation of the witnesses.

summary: Observation of a loud noise above a house: a clap of thunder.
description: On April 28, 2008, at approximately 4:10 a.m., a witness heard a muffled, rolling noise coming from the northeast. This noise transformed into a thunderous crash that lasted for 5 to 6 seconds as it passed over the house, startling the witness. The noise then moved away to the southwest. That same day, significant thunderstorm activity was recorded in the area. The witness heard a clap of thunder during a severe thunderstorm.

summary: Observation of rapid and silent movements of a flat circular object in the sky: observation of a light animation due to a disco laser.
description: On Sunday, April 27, 2008, at 4:17 a.m., a witness at his window was intrigued by the sight of a very rapid, circular, flattened luminous phenomenon. The object moved, notably in circles. No unusual noise was heard. No other reports of this phenomenon were collected. Given the shape of the object, similar to that produced by the projection of a laser on a layer of low clouds, the object's movements similar to those produced by the type of laser commonly used by nightclubs, the presence of a tail that can be considered the terminal part of the laser beam before it encounters the base of the clouds, the observation azimuth being the same as that towards which the nightclub producing the laser in question is located, the date (Saturday night to Sunday morning) coinciding with that of the use of said laser, and the visibility of the laser from the witness's home (verified on site by the gendarmerie), we can conclude that the object described by the witness is certainly an effect of the laser of the nightclub at Le Fashion Room, used regularly on Saturday nights from 11 p.m. to about 4 a.m. and reflected on the base of low clouds or local fog, probably present that day. This case is to be classified as A to A as an observation of a light animation.

summary: A brief account of the observation of a luminous phenomenon.
description: On April 25, 2008, at approximately 6:30 PM, a motorist observed a very bright light to the northwest. It appeared and disappeared while remaining stationary. The motorist lost sight of the phenomenon during his journey. No other witness accounts corroborate this brief observation, for which we lack further information.

summary: Observation of a light passing by and disappearing behind a hill: lack of information
description: On April 25, 2008, at approximately 8:30 PM, a witness and his wife were intrigued by the sight of a light source resembling a beacon above the hill opposite their terrace. The witness's observation could have several explanations: - a head-on view of an airplane. The powerful landing lights of the aircraft, seen in this case from about 10 km away, blinded the observer and prevented them from seeing the plane. As the aircraft descended, it disappeared behind the hill and veered westward; the beam of its landing lights then disappeared from the observer's view. The light traffic at the airport, especially at that time, could explain the observers' surprise. - a flash from an Iridium satellite could have produced the same effect of a point of light disappearing behind the hill. This somewhat unusual case is classified as "C" due to a lack of information to confirm either hypothesis.

summary: Strange objects in photos without visual observation.
description: witness reports that upon reviewing photos taken at the beach on April 23, 2008, around 4:15 PM, she noticed the presence of what appeared to be birds, a phenomenon she couldn't explain. It's always difficult to analyze photos containing unexplained birds without visual confirmation. However, in this case, they were likely birds that flew quickly into the camera's field of view. This is particularly evident in the first photo, where the body and wings are easily distinguishable; it's less obvious in the second, but by analogy, it's highly probable that it's the same phenomenon. After this observation was published on the website and following a message from a new witness, the object in the second photo was clearly identified as a frisbee (witness photo 2 retouched 100826), also visible in the hands of a thrower in the updated photo 1 (witness photo 1 retouched 100826). This case therefore consists of the observation of two different objects (probable observation of a bird in photo 1 and a frisbee in photo 2): the classification as case B remains unchanged with regard to the probable observation of a bird in photo 1.

summary: Probable reflection of the sun on a car windshield: lack of information.
description: On April 20 or 27, 2008, at 8:44 PM, a motorist took a photograph from his vehicle of a luminous phenomenon that intrigued him. The photograph reached GEIPAN (the French National Gendarmerie's Office for the Study of Unidentified Aerial Phenomena) through an indirect witness. The photograph provided shows a very probable reflection of the sun in the windshield and/or the camera lens, as well as water droplets on the windshield illuminated by the sun. This type of photograph, highlighting various "flare" phenomena and reflections, does not present any unusual characteristics. The witness's testimony is too brief, and the direct witness did not describe what he had seen with his own eyes. This case is classified as "C" due to a lack of information: no original photograph, no direct witness testimony.

summary: A stain on photographs without visual observation during the shooting process.
description: On April 20, 2008, a passenger in a car took a picture of clouds through the windshield. Upon reviewing the photographs, she noticed a spot that puzzled her, one she hadn't seen when the picture was taken. It's always difficult to analyze photos containing unexplained spots without visual confirmation. A defect in the windshield or an insect could also explain the spot; however, we lack more precise information in this case.

summary: Observations of three large bright points of yellow-orange colour moving slowly: probable observation of the passage of Thai lanterns.
description: On April 19, 2008, at approximately 9:20 PM, three people observed three large, bright yellow-orange points of light moving slowly in the sky. No unusual noises were heard during the observation. The points suddenly disappeared. One of the witnesses instinctively took a photograph; unfortunately, its poor quality and lack of reference points only serve to illustrate the witness's account. This account has all the characteristics of a sky lantern. However, the witness provides no terrestrial or celestial reference points that would allow for a more precise direction, which they estimate to be from southeast to northeast. This lack of precision prevents a firm conclusion, as the east-northeast wind does not align with the described direction. This case is classified as Class B, indicating a probable sky lantern sighting.

summary: Observation with the naked eye and then with a telescope of two lights above the city; 5 photographs taken handheld (significant camera shake): lack of information.
description: On the night of April 17-18, 2008, at 12:43 a.m., a resident of Rodez (12) observed two lights above the city from his home, heading south-southeast. He looked at them through a telescope and noticed that the lights were "vibrating." He then took five photographs: the first three spaced 15 to 20 seconds apart, and the last two after approximately 7 minutes. Only one witness account was collected. Several hypotheses were investigated: aeronautical, astronomical, or celebratory (see the investigation notes). Despite its limited strangeness and consistency (single witness, unusable photos), this case presents several characteristics that could suggest various explanatory hypotheses. Unfortunately, the long delay between the observation and its processing, the inaccuracies in the witness account, and the witness's failure to respond to GEIPAN's requests prevented any formal identification of the UFO. This case is class C, due to a lack of details.

summary: Observation of successive appearances of a luminous phenomenon in the form of flashes: mistaking for reflections of car headlights on a TV antenna.
description: On April 16, 2008, between 9:45 PM and 11:00 PM, a witness was puzzled to see a luminous phenomenon (in the form of flashes) between two rooftops in the southwest. The yellow-orange flashes appeared every two or three minutes within a limited area. While considered of low strangeness and moderate consistency (a single witness, but with a detailed and precise account), this case turned out to be a clear case of mistaken identity involving vehicle headlights reflecting off a neighboring house's antenna. This explanation was, in fact, provided by the witness himself after a similar observation later. This case is classified as Class A: mistaken identity involving reflections from car headlights.

summary: Observation of a reddish-orange light in the sky: mistaken for the moon at sunset.
description: On April 12, 2008, at 2:48 AM, a witness was intrigued by the presence of a peculiar reddish-orange light in the sky. The observation lasted two to three minutes before the phenomenon disappeared over the horizon. Due to its strangeness and lack of consistency (single witness, description of the UFO similar to the appearance of the Moon), this case appears to be a clear case of mistaken identity with the setting Moon, which was directly in the direction of observation. This case is classified as Class A, mistaken identity with the setting Moon.

summary: Observations of a stationary luminous phenomenon with strong scintillation: probable observation of Sirius.
description: On April 12, 2008, at approximately 10:00 PM, two witnesses were intrigued by a luminous phenomenon in the sky: a bright, round glow with a strong scintillation of several colors, predominantly blue, was stationary in the clear southwest sky. The witnesses had time to retrieve binoculars to improve their observation of this glow, which was larger and brighter than a star. The observation lasted about ten minutes. The day's star chart (see attached) indicates that Sirius, the brightest star in the sky (magnitude -1.44), was in the southwest sky at that time, 18 arcseconds above the horizon. When this star is visible low on the horizon, it often surprises witnesses, especially on clear days. It had disappeared, hidden behind the hill. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of the star Sirius. Because the direction of observation is not indicated very precisely, there remains a slight doubt about this hypothesis.

summary: Observation of the movement of a bright white point in the sky with an apparently irregular trajectory: observation of the passage of the international space station.
description: On April 4, 2008, at 10:28 PM, a motorist at the Mas d'Agenais rest area was intrigued by the unusual movement of a white object in the starry sky. The object moved along an irregular trajectory. The observation lasted approximately 50 seconds before the object gradually disappeared. Given the objective evidence gathered—namely, the presence of the International Space Station in the sky at the exact time of the observation, the witness's location, and the object's strong resemblance to a satellite, according to the witness himself—we can conclude that the object observed by the witness was most likely the International Space Station, and that the impression of the object stopping near airliners mentioned in the witness's testimony was a natural physiological ocular phenomenon (autostasis/micronystagmus). This case is classified as an eAe (Early Observatory).

summary: Observation of the rapid movement of two white dots.
description: Sometime in April 2008 (the main witness no longer remembers the exact date), two people observed two white lights moving rapidly around 7:45 PM. No noise was heard, but one of the witnesses observed a red and green flashing light (the colors are uncertain) between the two white lights. No other information was gathered about this sighting, which resembles a possible aircraft sighting, but for which we lack precise details.

summary: Observation of the movement of a point of light with acceleration and change of direction.
description: Recent testimony (May 31, 2010) of an earlier observation (date imprecise, April-May 2008). A witness reports seeing, for five seconds, the unusual movement of a point of light that accelerated and changed direction before disappearing. No other testimonies have been collected regarding this phenomenon. The imprecise details of this single testimony of an earlier observation make any investigation impossible.

summary: Observation of the movement of a group of luminous rings in the sky: probable light animation.
description: On March 31, 2008, between 10:20 and 10:30 a.m., a group of people at an airfield observed a mysterious luminous phenomenon: successive white rings of light moved across the sky. No sound was heard during the observation. A local witness stated that laser projectors used for advertising animations are frequently employed in this area by restaurants and nightclubs. GEIPAN therefore classified this case as "B": probable light show.

summary: Observation of the movement of several red light points: lack of information.
description: On March 30, 2008, at approximately 10:40 PM, a witness on his balcony was intrigued by the presence of several bright red lights on the horizon.
