Before moving, these lights emitted a bright white flash. They then gained altitude but were quickly obscured by a building. This observation is far too weak to allow for any conclusions. As it only involved a few lights observed from a distance for a few seconds, the strangeness is moderate, but the description is far too brief for a proper evaluation. An investigation long after the event would yield very little information. This case is classified as Class C due to a lack of independent witness statements and corroborating evidence.

summary: Observation of a luminous ball moving at very high speed.
description: On March 29, 2008, at approximately 9:30 PM, several witnesses observed a luminous phenomenon in the sky for three seconds. A very bright yellow ball moved at high speed from southwest to northeast. The witnesses noted a non-linear trajectory and an absence of noise. The luminous phenomenon disappeared abruptly. Based on their description of the phenomenon, these individuals likely witnessed an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observation of the movement of three dark objects in a South-North trajectory: probable observation of the passage of balloons of unknown origin.
description: On March 29, 2008, at approximately 7:05 or 7:10 PM, a witness was intrigued by the silent passage of three dark-colored circular objects across the sky. The objects were quickly obscured by the urban landscape. The observation lasted approximately 30 seconds. Based on the objective elements gathered, namely: - Rounded shape of the objects. - Movement of the objects along the same axis as the wind: South to North. - Estimated maximum size between approximately 1 m and 3 m. - Estimated maximum altitude at the zenith between approximately 30 m and 38.5 m. - Color and appearance of the objects similar to those of a transparent balloon. - Undefined leaching zone. - Three objects observed. - Significant discrepancy between the altitude estimates given by the primary witness and the calculations performed in this report. We can conclude that the objects described by the witness were wind-borne objects: balloons whose nature and location could not be determined. This case should be classified as a probable observation of balloons of unknown origin.

summary: Fireball falls with a trail.
description: On March 25, 2008, at 9:15 PM, a witness observed a fireball falling, followed by a very long tail. This orange-colored object was moving from west to north on a downward trajectory. The observation lasted 8 seconds. This person likely witnessed an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observation of silent and successive passages of a "fireball": probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On March 15, 2008, between 10:20 PM and 10:30 PM, two witnesses observed three silent and successive passages of a luminous phenomenon described as a "fireball." The witness's description (a shimmering ball), the spacing between the observations, the movement consistent with the prevailing wind direction (from the East), and the time and day of the week (Saturday evening) are consistent with the observation of Thai lanterns. This case is classified as "B": probable observation of three Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of an unexplained stain on a photograph.
description: On March 10, 2008, an amateur photographer sent GEIPAN a photograph taken from his window in Paris, one of a series of five high-quality photos taken in rapid succession. This photograph shows an elliptical, almost round object, dark on the lower part and light on top. The object is quite sharp and appears to be illuminated by the sun. The investigation was entrusted to Mr. Jean Marc Gillot, IPN in Paris (see the IPN report). Reordering the photos, particularly photos 4 and 5, clearly shows that a pigeon coming from the witness's left passed into the frame of photo 4 before diving towards a window and being captured in photo 5. The photographs taken are therefore indeed of a pigeon, whose very round shape and metallic appearance misled the witness.

summary: A blue (or orange, according to witnesses) ball was observed moving rapidly at low altitude.
description: On March 1, 2008, at approximately 11:50 PM, several people observed a luminous phenomenon at low altitude in the sky for a few seconds. A colored, circular object moved horizontally in an east-west direction. This sphere then followed a downward trajectory and disappeared in a flash of light seen by some witnesses. No trace of it was found on the ground. These individuals witnessed what was likely an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Successive observations of the movement of luminous balls descending along a hill towards a stream: probable observations of geomagnetic luminous phenomena.
description: witness reported several sightings of luminous phenomena seen from his home (he indicated in his police report the date as February 22, 2008, around 10 or 11 p.m., but during the interview with the investigator, he refined the date to February 29 at 9:30 p.m.). The witness thus saw white "fireballs" three times in the evening over two years. These descended from the hillside to a stream. No other witness statements were collected. No traces of fire were found on the ground. After consulting an expert on transient atmospheric luminous phenomena (lightning, plasmas), it appears that all parameters are consistent with geomagnetic luminous phenomena ("Earthballs" or "Earthlights") linked to geological faults: the presence of power lines and watercourses oriented in the direction of the spheres' flow. GEIPAN classifies this case as B e, indicating highly probable observations of geomagnetic luminous phenomena.

summary: Observation of the slow and silent movement of two round, white objects in the sky: lack of information
description: On February 18, 2008, at 4:21 PM, a witness observed two round, white objects in the sky above a mountain range. The witness took a photograph. No other reports were collected regarding this phenomenon (see the investigation report). Due to its limited strangeness and insufficient consistency, no conclusions can be drawn from this case. This case is classified as Class C due to a lack of information and corroboration.

summary: Observation of the passage at very high speed of an orange ball in a descending trajectory: probable observation of a natural atmospheric reentry (bolide).
description: On February 13, 2008, at approximately 1:25 AM, a witness waking up in the middle of the night observed a large orange ball moving at very high speed across the sky from their home. The observation lasted only a few seconds, and the UFO disappeared immediately. Only one witness account was recorded. Due to its low oddity and lack of consistency (single witness, very short observation duration), this case appears to be a very likely case of misidentification as a natural fireball. However, the absence of independent witness accounts or a capture by an all-sky camera prevents formal confirmation of this hypothesis. This case is classified as Class B, a probable case of misidentification as a natural atmospheric reentry (fireball).

summary: Observation of two particular phenomena: an unknown stationary craft and a fireball: lack of information.
description: On February 7, 2008, at approximately 7:10 PM, a witness observed what he described as a spacecraft with a red and white light in the sky. Simultaneously, a huge fireball fell to the right of this first UFO, on a downward trajectory. The observation lasted approximately 12 seconds. No other reports were collected. Of moderate strangeness but with weak consistency (single witness, brief testimony, contradictions, short observation), this case is too incomplete to be classified. The observation consists of a probable simultaneous sighting of a fireball and a possible sighting of an aircraft. Unfortunately, the latter cannot be verified due to a significant delay in transmission to GEIPAN. This case is classified as Class C due to a lack of data.

summary: probable atmospheric re-entry
description: On February 1, 2008, at approximately 6:30 PM, a witness observed a white trail in the sky, about 30 arcseconds above the horizon, moving south-southeast. A few seconds later, the white trail disappeared from view, but the witness observed smoke that gradually dissipated. The local press reported similar observations that day. This person likely witnessed an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observations of the presumed fall of a meteorite.
description: On January 25, 2008, at approximately 6:15 PM, numerous witnesses, primarily in southwestern France, observed a bright object in the sky. The investigation conducted by GEIPAN (the French National Center for Experimental and Analysis for Nuclear Research) failed to confirm the hypothesis of atmospheric reentry of space debris, and the accepted hypothesis was that of a meteorite. More than 170 eyewitness accounts were collected, allowing investigators to establish a trajectory and a probable impact point east of Albi. Although several witnesses brought stones found after the sighting to GEIPAN, no meteorite debris was recovered.

summary: Observation of a white light making two circles and accompanied by a rumbling sound: probable observation of the passage of a military aircraft on a training exercise.
description: On January 24, 2008, at 1:15 a.m., a witness observed a white light at high altitude. It traced two circles in the sky and then disappeared. During the observation, a loud rumbling noise was heard. The witness's description clearly suggested an aircraft. The movement of the light was, however, surprising. But the witness was near a military air training area (see attached map, taken from the "Very Low Altitude Defense Network Map" RTBA): a military aircraft could very well exhibit this behavior during maneuvers. This case is classified as "B": probable observation of a military aircraft during maneuvers.

summary: Successive observations of luminous phenomena.
description: A witness briefly reported, via email, successive observations (between 2007 and 2008) of luminous phenomena moving across the sky. The witness provided no further details about the specific observations.

summary: orange light phenomenon on photograph (TMP).
description: On January 1, 2008, a motorist took photos of the Puy de Dôme from inside his car with his mobile phone. When he looked at them a month later, he noticed a luminous phenomenon he couldn't explain and sent his photographs to GEIPAN. It turned out to be a reflection of a light inside the vehicle (dome light or other).

summary: observation of the movement of a luminous phenomenon.
description: witness reported, without any details about the observation, the movement of a luminous phenomenon (no date specified: we date the event to the date of the report, i.e., October 29, 2008). Despite our requests, the witness provided no further information about this phenomenon.
